create.name: Ken Honda
create.bio:
Ken Honda is a Japanese author and teacher whose work centres on the emotional and spiritual side of our relationship with money. As a boy he helped out in his father's accounting practice and noticed that some clients seemed at ease with money while others were driven and restless, a contrast that became the thread of his later work. After running consulting and accounting businesses he stepped back from them in his late twenties to spend time with his young daughter, and began to write. He has since published more than a hundred books in Japanese, where he is often called the Zen Millionaire, and in English he is known for Happy Money, which Simon & Schuster brought out in 2019, and True Wealth, a teaching story published by Hay House in 2024.

His central idea is that money carries the feeling with which it is earned, given and spent, and that simple gratitude, often expressed in the word arigato, changes how it moves through a life. He also writes about Lifework, the idea of shaping your work around the person you feel called to be. He teaches through short talks on his YouTube channel, keynote talks for audiences around the world, a twelve-week online group programme on true wealth and a free starter guide, and he has taught online courses with The Shift Network.
